title: tpall/DRAM: DRAM2-v, a DRAM-v (viral mode) reimplementation for the DRAM2 Nextflow workflow
description:
A fork of WrightonLabCSU/DRAM that adds viral-mode (DRAM-v) annotation to the DRAM2 Nextflow workflow, referred to as DRAM2-v. Viral mode was not available in the upstream Nextflow workflow at the time of this work.

This snapshot archives the exact revision used for the auxiliary-metabolic-gene analysis of a vOTU catalogue in the accompanying manuscript. It corresponds to commit 0c828513fa17ebd0857e83ab6a372b768f41d84c of this fork, plus archival metadata files only; no code differs.

Additions over upstream include: per-gene DRAM-v amg_flags and is_transposon; the v1 auxiliary_score; an adapter allowing that score to be computed from geNomad output rather than requiring VirSorter; an essential_viral_function annotation and corresponding N flag following Martin et al. 2025 (doi:10.1038/s41564-025-02095-4); and an --amg_only distillation mode. Flag semantics are ported from DRAM v1 mag_annotator/annotate_vgfs.py.

Note on annotation settings: this revision uses a Z-independent bit-score prefilter (-T 10 --domT 10) for HMM searches in place of the upstream e-value prefilter, which was required to make pooled multi-genome HMM searches produce results identical to per-genome searches. This applies to every HMM database. For KOfam the downstream parser then applies per-profile bit-score thresholds, but the VOGdb annotation file carries no threshold column, so VOGdb hits are retained at the bit-score floor of 10 with no further significance filtering. Users comparing against upstream defaults should account for this.

DRAM itself is the work of the Wrighton Lab and its contributors; see the upstream repository and Shaffer et al. 2020 (doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa621). This archive covers the fork's modifications only and is redistributed under the same GPL-3.0 license.
